# Sign Pumpkin plugin

Use this action after your workflow builds a plugin `.wasm` file. It adds Pumpkin's Ed25519
signature and release metadata to the file in place; it doesn't build the plugin. Run your publish
or distribution step against the signed file.

<!-- docs:begin reference -->
<!-- Generated by pumpkin-plugins-docs from package, action, extension, and component docs metadata. Run `pnpm readme`. -->

See the [action guide](https://filiphsps.github.io/pumpkin-plugins/actions/sign-pumpkin-plugin/docs/) and [API reference](https://filiphsps.github.io/pumpkin-plugins/api/actions/sign-pumpkin-plugin/) on the documentation site.
<!-- docs:end reference -->

```yaml
steps:
  - uses: filiphsps/pumpkin-plugins/actions/sign-pumpkin-plugin@sign-pumpkin-plugin-v0.0.4
    with:
      plugin-name: MyPlugin
      version: 1.2.3
      wasm-file: dist/my-plugin.wasm
      developer-name: My Name
      signing-key: ${{ secrets.PLUGIN_SIGNING_KEY }}
```

This example signs `dist/my-plugin.wasm` as `MyPlugin` version `1.2.3`. The tag in `uses` is this
action's Release Please version; it changes independently of the plugin version in `version`.

Before writing the file, the action replaces any existing signing sections and verifies the new
signature. If a sibling `<wasm-file>.sha256` checksum file exists, it updates that checksum to match
the signed bytes. It uses the shared `@pumpkin-plugins/signing` implementation and the Node 24 runtime
declared in [`action.yml`](action.yml), so you don't need a separate build or runner setup step.

For a release with several plugins, list each plugin's name, version, and `.wasm` path in a JSON
manifest instead of setting the three single-file inputs:

```json
[
  { "plugin-name": "MyPlugin", "version": "1.2.3", "wasm-file": "dist/my-plugin.wasm" }
]
```

Pass the manifest path through `plugins-manifest`. The developer name and signing key still apply to
every entry:

```yaml
steps:
  - uses: filiphsps/pumpkin-plugins/actions/sign-pumpkin-plugin@sign-pumpkin-plugin-v0.0.4
    with:
      plugins-manifest: dist/plugins.json
      developer-name: My Name
      signing-key: ${{ secrets.PLUGIN_SIGNING_KEY }}
```

The action prepares every signature before it writes any files, so a missing file or invalid
manifest entry won't leave earlier plugins signed while later ones fail.

## Inputs

<!-- action-inputs:start -->
| Input | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `plugin-name` | No |  | Single-file mode; exact plugin name embedded in the signature metadata |
| `version` | No |  | Single-file mode; plugin version embedded without a leading v |
| `wasm-file` | No |  | Single-file mode; path to the plugin .wasm file to sign |
| `plugins-manifest` | No |  | Batch mode; JSON array of plugin-name, version, and wasm-file entries instead of single-file inputs |
| `developer-name` | Yes |  | Developer name embedded in signed metadata; required in either mode |
| `signing-key` | No |  | 32-byte Ed25519 secret seed as 64 hexadecimal characters; required unless warn is true |
| `warn` | No | `false` | Warn and leave the file unchanged when signing-key is empty instead of failing |
<!-- action-inputs:end -->

## Outputs

<!-- action-outputs:start -->
This action has no outputs.
<!-- action-outputs:end -->

Store the signing key in a protected GitHub secret. It must be a 32-byte Ed25519 seed written as 64
hexadecimal characters. If a workflow should continue without signing when the key is empty, set
`warn: true`; the action warns and leaves each file unchanged. This option only skips an empty key:
a malformed key, missing or invalid WebAssembly file, or failed signature verification still fails.
